questions.q: Which three broad mechanisms does this lesson say data moves across an enterprise landscape through?
options: Batch, event-driven, and virtualized
Encrypted, tokenized, and masked
Public, Internal, and Confidential
Request and Reply, Fire and Forget, and Remote Call-In
questions.explain: The lesson describes batch (scheduled, bulk movement), event-driven (asynchronous, near-real-time), and virtualized (read live at query time, never moved) as the three broad mechanisms underlying enterprise data flows.

questions.q: What does Change Data Capture (CDC) do, per this lesson?
options: It encrypts field values at rest
It publishes change events automatically whenever a supported record is created, updated, deleted, or undeleted
It replaces the need for any batch data movement entirely
It is a tool exclusively for managing sandbox refresh schedules
questions.explain: CDC publishes change events for record creation, update, deletion, and undeletion on custom objects and a defined subset of standard objects, letting subscribers react without polling Salesforce repeatedly.

questions.q: How does this lesson distinguish Platform Events from Change Data Capture?
options: They are identical in every respect with no meaningful distinction
Platform Events are custom-defined events tied to business logic (not necessarily one-to-one with a record change), while CDC is specifically tied to record creation/update/delete/undelete
Platform Events only work with Big Objects, while CDC only works with standard objects
Platform Events are synchronous, while CDC is the only asynchronous mechanism on the platform
questions.explain: The lesson distinguishes Platform Events as custom-defined business-logic events (such as 'a case was escalated') that aren't necessarily tied one-to-one to a record change, whereas CDC is specifically about record-level change events.

questions.q: What trade-off does this lesson say Big Objects make to achieve very high storage scale?
options: They cost nothing extra but have no trade-off whatsoever
They give up standard platform automation (no triggers, no Flow, no out-of-the-box page layouts) in exchange for massive storage scale outside standard storage limits
They can only be used for data that will never be queried again
They automatically delete themselves after one year
questions.explain: The lesson states Big Objects don't support standard platform automation (triggers, Flow, out-of-the-box layouts), typically requiring a custom Lightning web component for display -- a deliberate trade for scale and storage efficiency.

questions.q: Per this lesson's 'requirement first, technology second' discipline, which mechanism fits a business need where sales reps must see live inventory levels from a warehouse system that should never be duplicated into Salesforce?
options: Batch, refreshed nightly
Event-driven Platform Events
Virtualization, such as through Salesforce Connect's external objects
Big Objects
questions.explain: A requirement that data should never actually live inside Salesforce, but still needs to be visible live, points directly to virtualization -- reading the data live at query time from its source, which is what Salesforce Connect's external objects are built for.
